source_read: PDF p. 1 (PDFs/MDMA/Mahase_2024_ThreePapersRetractedFDA.pdf): the one-page news article read in full with its 7 references and rendered at 110 dpi; p. 2 is a permissions notice. Compared with the three retraction notes, read in full on link.springer.com in my own browser tab the same day. Step 1 (blind extraction) not run this round, per the round brief.

design.note: A staff news report; narrative-review is the schema's closest value. Five unheaded opening paragraphs and seven under 'FDA rejects Lykos Therapeutics' application' confirmed on the rendered page.

instrument.note: none-applicable with the editors' narrative-review checklist.

key_findings.correction: The notices did not say what the violations were; reports (ref 4, a New York Times article of 12 August 2024; ref 5, a 2019 MAPS statement announcing an ethical violation by former MAPS-sponsored investigators) suggest that an investigator at one study site had an unethical sexual relationship with a trial participant; in a 2018 lawsuit settled out of court the participant said she had been sexually assaulted, and the investigator said the relationship was consensual (ref 6, a CBC report of March 2022).
key_findings.note: The article says 'reports suggest'; only ref 4 is a press report. Ref 5 is the sponsor's own public statement, its URL dated 24 May 2019.
Checked against the notices: two authors (feduccia_2024, MAPS PBC only) and 'several of the authors' (jerome_2024, mithoefer_2024).
The source says 'the majority of experts'; ref 7 is the final summary minutes, dated 30 July 2024.
Consistent with the notices: Amy Emerson is an author of the Mithoefer and Jerome articles, not the Feduccia one.
DOIs and PMIDs as printed; the DOIs match the notices' pages and Crossref records.

reporting_issues.note: Verified on the notices: of those who responded, 6 of 8, 4 of 5 and 3 of 4 authors disagreed with the retraction.

risk_of_bias.note: I agree with every domain and the overall.

domains.note: On the checklist's letter a news report has no search and would be high, as the three commentaries are; some-concerns is defensible because the article goes to the primary documents for both events (the notices and the committee minutes) rather than choosing sources to fit a thesis. A single-domain difference at most.

domains.domain: Reliance on the authors' own studies
Balance of perspectives on the retractions and the FDA decision
domains.note: One more point for the note: the chief executive quoted at length is, by elimination from the notices' named responders, among the authors who did not respond to the publisher about the retraction of both her papers.

overall.note: Some concerns, matching the worst domains.

interpretation_gap.note: Minor. The headline's 'as' is accurate in time (the two events fell within days); the text does not tie the retractions to the FDA review.

missed: Ref 5 is the sponsor's own 2019 public statement of an ethical violation by former MAPS-sponsored investigators (URL dated 24 May 2019), not a press report. With the notices' dates this gives a timeline worth recording: the statement came 17 days after the first retracted article was published online (7 May 2019) and before the other two (4 June and 21 November 2020).
Ref 6's title refers to a trial in British Columbia; the article never names the site, and the notices call it MP4. The card should not equate the two without a source.

Amy Emerson, quoted at length as chief executive, is among the 'remaining authors' who did not respond to the publisher about either retraction of her papers (by elimination from the authors each notice names: Hamilton and Emerson for Mithoefer et al.; Wang, Hamilton and Emerson for Jerome et al.).
